app.setup.title_default.why: States the current state plainly, using the same enabled/disabled adjective the app uses elsewhere.

app.setup.title_failed.why: “تعذّر” is the standard Arabic hedge verb for a failed check (as in تعذّر الاتصال), keeping this distinct from a definite off-state.

app.setup.detail_default.s: عند تفعيلها، لا يخطف أي موقع محمي ضغطاتك بعد الآن.
app.setup.detail_default.back: Once enabled, no protected site hijacks your taps anymore.
app.setup.detail_default.why: States the payoff plainly with a concrete verb (يخطف, hijacks) rather than a slogan.

app.setup.detail_failed.s: تعذّر التأكد الآن، وسيلاحظ التطبيق تفعيل الإضافة في Safari بمجرد حدوثه.
app.setup.detail_failed.back: Confirming failed now, and the app will notice enabling the extension in Safari once it happens.
app.setup.detail_failed.why: Plain, no jargon or error code; promises automatic detection so the person never needs to come back and refresh.

app.setup.open_button.why: Names the exact action generically enough to work verbatim on both the setup screen and the welcome sheet.

app.welcome.heading.why: The standard Arabic welcome formula (مرحبًا بك في X); the one place in the product allowed a warmer register.

app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.tit.why: Concrete two-word noun phrase naming the trick, parallel in shape to the other four feature titles.

app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.s: قد تُخفي الصفحة طبقة فوقها، فتصل ضغطتك إلى شيء آخر غير الذي تراه.
app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.back: The page may hide a layer over itself, so your tap reaches something other than what you see.
app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.why: Describes what the person experiences (the tap lands elsewhere), not the underlying script mechanism.

app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.title.why: Concrete noun phrase naming the trick, parallel to the sibling titles.

app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.s: تُغيّر بعض الصفحات وجهة الرابط بين ضغطك وإفلاته، فلا تصل حيث توقعت.
app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.back: Some pages change the link's destination between your press and its release, so you don't arrive where you expected.
app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.why: Plain description of the experienced effect, matching the sibling detail sentences' register and length.

app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.ti.why: Concrete noun phrase for the trick, parallel to the sibling titles.

app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.s: مع الحماية، لا يفتح تبويب جديد إلا فيما ضغطت عليه فعلًا، بلا إضافات خفية.
app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.back: With protection, no new tab opens except to what you actually pressed, without hidden additions.
app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.why: Framed as a promise per the brief, rather than a description of the trick itself.

app.welcome.feature.every_destination.ti.why: Names the feature as a noun (a log of destinations), matching the checklist icon and sibling title shape.

app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.s: لكل وجهة سجل خاص، تختار فيه السماح أو الحظر هنا أو في كل مكان.
app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.back: Every destination has its own record, in which you choose allow or block, here or everywhere.
app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.why: Concrete description of the review-and-choose mechanic, kept within the short detail budget.

app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.t.why: Mirrors the concept directly as a short noun phrase, parallel to the sibling titles.

app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.s: اضغط زر Undirect في شريط أدوات Safari لتفعيل الحماية على ذلك الموقع فقط.
app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.back: Press the Undirect button in Safari's toolbar to enable protection on that site only.
app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.why: States the exact mechanism (the toolbar button) concretely, matching sibling detail register.

app.nav.guarded_sites.why: Short two-word noun phrase using the established “protected” adjective; works as both sidebar label and nav title.

app.nav.settings.why: Apple's own Arabic term for Settings, which wins over any invented synonym.

app.nav.app_title.why: Brand name, left untranslated per the product's own proper-noun convention.

app.rules.grouping.everywhere.why: The idiomatic Arabic filter-tab word contrasting with “by X”, matching how Apple's own Settings pairs “الكل” against “حسب التطبيق”.

app.rules.grouping.by_site.why: Direct opposite of “الكل”, standard “by X” filter phrasing, reading as a clear contrasting pair beside it.

app.rules.empty_no_app.title.why: Frames this as a first-contact/wiring state (the extension hasn't reported anything), distinct from an empty-content state.

app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.s: افتح أي صفحة في Safari مرة، وستظهر البيانات هنا.
app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.back: Open any page in Safari once, and the data will appear here.
app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.why: Simple imperative fix with no setting to change, shared verbatim between the two screens as specified.

app.rules.empty_no_rules.title.why: Plain, short statement contrasting with the wiring-state title above it.

app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.s: تظهر الوجهة هنا فقط بعد أن تسمح بها أو تحظرها.
app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.back: The destination appears here only after you allow or block it.
app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.why: States precisely when a row is created: only after an explicit decision, not merely being seen.

app.rules.footer.lifetime_count.why: Placeholder placed where Arabic puts the counted noun after the numeral; this single string stands in for the “other” form of the full CLDR plural set a String Catalog would carry (zero/one/two/few/many/other), since only one string slot exists here.

app.rules.row.state_blocked.why: Invariant one-word status chip, masculine default per Arabic UI convention, pairing cleanly with state_allowed.

app.rules.row.action_allow.why: Apple's own Arabic term for the “Allow” action (as used in iOS permission prompts), reused as a verbal-noun menu item.

app.rules.row.action_block.why: Matching verbal-noun counterpart to action_allow, pairing as Apple's own Allow/Block idiom.

app.rules.row.help_tooltip.s: اختيار السماح بهذه الوجهة أو حظرها
app.rules.row.help_tooltip.back: Choosing to allow this destination or block it
app.rules.row.help_tooltip.why: Concise verbal-noun tooltip phrase, matching macOS's own terse .help style.

app.rules.row.use_default.why: Names clearing the explicit rule as reverting to the default policy, not setting a new verdict.

app.watched.empty.title.why: Plain statement that no site has been switched on, matching the sibling empty-state title shape.

app.watched.empty.detail.s: اضغط زر Undirect في شريط أدوات Safari عند زيارة موقع يسيء التصرف.
app.watched.empty.detail.back: Press the Undirect button in Safari's toolbar when visiting a site that misbehaves.
app.watched.empty.detail.why: Concrete first-use instruction naming the exact button and the moment to use it.

app.watched.footer.s: تُضاف المواقع من زر Undirect في Safari فقط، لا من هنا.
app.watched.footer.back: Sites are added only from the Undirect button in Safari, not from here.
app.watched.footer.why: States the one-way limitation plainly: this screen removes sites but cannot add them.

app.watched.row.guarded_badge.why: One-word read-only status, matching the “protected” adjective used throughout the vocabulary.

app.watched.row.stop_button.why: Short imperative verb suitable for a small trailing row button.

app.watched.row.stop_tooltip.why: Concise verbal-noun tooltip describing exactly what the button under the pointer does.

app.settings.guard_toggle.why: The vocabulary's core noun (“guard”) as the master toggle's one-word label.

app.settings.state_on.why: Apple's own system word for a toggle's on state, generic enough for both the Guard row and the page-note row.

app.settings.state_off.why: Apple's own system word for a toggle's off state, clear opposite of state_on.

app.settings.mode_heading.why: Introduces the choice of which sites the guard runs on, as a short picker/section header.

app.settings.mode_watched.why: Framed from the person's own action (“you enable”) rather than a technical mode name, per the brief.

app.settings.mode_everywhere.why: Short two-word option meaning the guard runs automatically on every site.

app.settings.banner_toggle.why: Names exactly what the toggle draws (an on-page note), matching the “page note” vocabulary concept.

app.settings.policy_heading.back: The default policy for new destinations
app.settings.policy_heading.why: Introduces the default-policy choice using the vocabulary's own “default policy” term, framing an unrated destination as “new”.

app.settings.policy_block.why: Short imperative-phrase option meaning an unrated destination is stopped by default.

app.settings.policy_allow.why: Clear opposite of policy_block, same two-word shape.

ext.meta.name.why: Brand name, left untranslated, matching app.nav.app_title.

ext.meta.description.s: يمنع Undirect المواقع من استغلال ضغطاتك لفتح صفحات أو إعادة توجيهك دون إذنك.
ext.meta.description.back: Undirect prevents sites from exploiting your taps to open pages or redirect you without your permission.
ext.meta.description.why: Slightly more explanatory than the in-app copy, since this is often the first thing a prospective user reads, per the brief's register note.

ext.meta.app_title.why: Fallback stand-in for the site name; since it is the product's own name, it stays the brand word.

ext.toolbar.tooltip_on.back: Protection is enabled on this site
ext.toolbar.tooltip_on.why: States the current state plainly as the toolbar icon's tooltip/accessible name.

ext.toolbar.tooltip_off.back: Protection is off, press to enable
ext.toolbar.tooltip_off.why: Combines the state with the implied call to action in one tooltip, since a press here is the one-tap way to start guarding.

ext.toolbar.tooltip_no_site.why: Brief explanation that there is nothing to guard on a tab with no website loaded.

ext.popup.no_site_title.why: Terse empty-state headline beside a small icon, matching sibling empty-state title lengths.

ext.popup.no_site_body.s: افتح موقعًا، ثم اضغط هنا لحمايته.
ext.popup.no_site_body.back: Open a site, then press here to protect it.
ext.popup.no_site_body.why: Keeps “here” as a self-reference to the button the popup hangs off, per the brief's note, rather than translating it as a place.

ext.popup.watch_switch_label.s: تفعيل الحماية أو إيقافها لهذا الموقع
ext.popup.watch_switch_label.back: Turning protection on or off for this site
ext.popup.watch_switch_label.why: Screen-reader-only label spelling out the switch's function, since the visible row shows only the site name.

ext.popup.watch_unknown.why: Brief reason the switch is disabled: there is no actual page to guard.

ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.s: الحماية مفعّلة على كل موقع من الإعدادات.
ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.back: Protection is enabled on every site from Settings.
ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.why: Explains the switch is redundant because the everywhere-mode setting already covers this site.

ext.popup.watch_master_off.back: Protection is completely off from Settings
ext.popup.watch_master_off.why: Attributes the disabled switch to the master switch, not to anything about this particular site.

ext.popup.watch_on.s: الحماية مفعّلة هنا، إيقافها يعيد تحميل الصفحة.
ext.popup.watch_on.back: Protection is enabled here, turning it off reloads the page.
ext.popup.watch_on.why: States the current state, then the reload warning as one clause, mirroring watch_off's shape.

ext.popup.watch_off.s: الحماية متوقفة هنا، تفعيلها يعيد تحميل الصفحة.
ext.popup.watch_off.back: Protection is off here, turning it on reloads the page.
ext.popup.watch_off.why: Mirrors watch_on's exact sentence shape, swapping state and action, so the pair reads as before/after.

ext.popup.page_heading.why: Short two-word heading, matching the vocabulary's site-vs-page distinction.

ext.popup.page_off.s: لا شيء يُرصد هنا، فالحماية متوقفة على هذا الموقع.
ext.popup.page_off.back: Nothing is tracked here, since protection is off on this site.
ext.popup.page_off.why: Dead key as of 2026-09-22 per the brief; written to match the voice of the sibling page-section states in case it is ever wired up.

ext.popup.page_quiet.s: لم تحاول هذه الصفحة الوصول إلى موقع آخر.
ext.popup.page_quiet.back: This page hasn't tried to reach another site.
ext.popup.page_quiet.why: Plain statement that nothing on this page has reached outward so far.

ext.popup.page_empty.why: Dead key per the brief, treated as a near-synonym of page_quiet rather than a distinct phrasing.

ext.popup.stopped_one.why: Arabic's “one” category names the item without a digit; paired with stopped_other's $COUNT$ + plural noun for every other count.

ext.popup.stopped_other.why: General/plural form covering 0, 2-10 and 11+ with the plural noun محاولات; a full six-category CLDR set isn't available in this two-slot i18n scheme, so this single form approximates all non-one counts.

ext.popup.seen_one.why: Mirrors stopped_one's no-digit “one” phrasing, but with the broader verb “رُصدت/سُجّلت” since ‘seen’ covers both blocked and allowed attempts.

ext.popup.seen_other.why: Plural counterpart to seen_one, same $COUNT$ + plural-noun approximation as stopped_other.

ext.popup.tries_one.why: Terse inline fragment (no full sentence) to sit alongside the scope/kind/reason fragments in the same detail line.

ext.popup.tries_other.why: Plural inline fragment counterpart to tries_one, same terse shape.

ext.popup.recipe_heading.why: Short lead-in fragment reading naturally before the colon and the fix's own name, as “${heading}: ${text}” in code.

ext.state.blocked.why: Invariant one-word status chip (masculine default), the most-reused word in the extension; combines cleanly with the following scope fragment.

ext.state.allowed.why: Clear opposite of state.blocked, same invariant chip shape.

ext.state.removed.why: Passive-verb status chip for a trap taken off the page directly, parallel in shape to Blocked/Allowed but with no destination to rule on.

ext.scope.here.why: Composed as ‘${verdict} ${scope}’ in code; Arabic reads naturally in the same order as English (محظور على هذا الموقع), so no reordering is needed.

ext.scope.everywhere.why: One-word adverb fills the single-word budget where the literal “everywhere” would need three Arabic words; composes as ‘${verdict} عالميًا’.

ext.scope.default.why: Single Arabic adverb natively expressing “by default”, composing as ‘${verdict} افتراضيًا’ (e.g. محظور افتراضيًا).

ext.action.allow_here.why: Complete, unambiguous menu option scoped to the current site.

ext.action.allow_everywhere.why: Reuses “عالميًا” (globally) from ext.scope.everywhere for terminology consistency across the popup.

ext.action.block_here.why: Counterpart to allow_here, same scoped shape.

ext.action.block_everywhere.why: Counterpart to allow_everywhere, reusing “عالميًا” for consistency.

ext.popup.policy_heading.back: The default policy for unrated destinations
ext.popup.policy_heading.why: Same concept as app.settings.policy_heading, phrased consistently so the two read as the same idea across app and extension.

ext.policy.block.why: Same wording as app.settings.policy_block for consistency across surfaces.

ext.policy.allow.why: Same wording as app.settings.policy_allow for consistency across surfaces.

ext.popup.bridge_warning.s: تمنع سياسة الأمان في هذه الصفحة جزءًا من الحماية، فتبقى الحماية هنا جزئية فقط.
ext.popup.bridge_warning.back: This page's security policy prevents part of protection, so protection here stays only partial.
ext.popup.bridge_warning.why: Frames the limitation as belonging to this one page's own settings, not a bug or a setting to fix, per the brief.

ext.kind.click_catcher.why: Names the invisible clickable element concretely; terse noun phrase for the comma-joined tag list.

ext.kind.overlay.why: Broader than click_catcher: any see-through element over the page, not specifically something clickable.

ext.kind.synthetic_click.why: Names a click the page's own script dispatched itself, not a real press from the person.

ext.kind.window_open.why: Standard Arabic term for a script-opened pop-up window.

ext.kind.form_submit.why: Names the hidden-form-submission trick tersely, matching sibling tag length.

ext.kind.href_swap.why: Names the link-retargeting trick, three words matching its budget.

ext.kind.redirect.why: Names the core same-tab redirect trick as a noun phrase, distinct from the generic “redirect” word.

ext.kind.pop_tab.why: Names the tab-under trick, distinct from window_open's explicit window call.

ext.kind.network_rule.why: Names the strongest, earliest kind of block: stopped before the request ever reached the page.

ext.reason.way_back.back: It includes a way back to the site
ext.reason.way_back.why: Brief footnote explaining the round-trip signal that let this redirect through.

ext.reason.sized.back: It opened at a deliberate size
ext.reason.sized.why: Short passive-verb footnote naming the specific-size signal that let this window through.

ext.reason.took_press.back: It took a press meant for something else
ext.reason.took_press.why: Very short footnote (15-25 char budget) naming the core hijack pattern tersely.

ext.reason.default_allow.why: Very short footnote stating there was simply no rule against this destination.

ext.reason.own_code.back: The site's own code opened it
ext.reason.own_code.why: Short footnote naming the site's own script as the one vouching for the window.

ext.popup.rules_link.why: One-word section name reused as nav row, header title, and back-button accessibility label.

ext.popup.back_link.why: One-word accessible label naming the destination (the popup's main view) rather than the generic verb “back”, read aloud with no visual context.

ext.rules.everywhere_heading.why: Section heading for rules that apply to every guarded site, a separate translation unit from app.rules.grouping.everywhere but the same concept.

ext.rules.by_site_heading.why: Clear counterpart to everywhere_heading, naming per-site rules.

ext.action.allow.why: Same word as action_allow_here/everywhere but without a scope suffix, since scope is already fixed by which section list the row sits in.

ext.action.block.why: Counterpart to action.allow, same simplified context.

ext.action.clear.why: Same underlying action as app.rules.row.use_default (clearing the explicit rule), phrased compactly for the tighter popup menu.

ext.popup.settings_heading.why: Same Apple system term used for the extension's own Settings section, a separate translation unit from the container app's Settings screen but reading identically to the user.

ext.settings.guard_label.why: Same one-word term as app.settings.guard_toggle, reused for both the visible row label and the sr-only switch label.

ext.settings.guard_on.why: Same Apple toggle term as app.settings.state_on, kept consistent across app and extension.

ext.settings.guard_off.why: Same Apple toggle term as app.settings.state_off.

ext.settings.mode_heading.why: Same wording as app.settings.mode_heading for cross-surface consistency.

ext.settings.mode_watched.why: Same wording as app.settings.mode_watched for cross-surface consistency.

ext.settings.mode_everywhere.why: Same wording as app.settings.mode_everywhere for cross-surface consistency.

ext.settings.banner_toggle.why: Same concept as app.settings.banner_toggle, compressed to two words to fit the popup's tighter toggle row.

ext.action.report.why: Slightly over the two-word budget to keep the nav row unambiguous; a bare “إبلاغ” alone reads as incomplete in Arabic.
